claims.title: San Agustin megaliths
claims.summary: In the upper Magdalena valley, the San Agustin culture carves the largest assemblage of monumental religious statuary in South America, later a UNESCO World Heritage site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Colombia: From the goldsmiths of the Muisca and the legend of El Dorado to a Spanish viceroyalty, the cradle of Bolivar's republic, and a modern nation that fought its way through partisan wars and a long armed conflict toward peace.", terralore.co/country/COL/chronicle#ev-1bce-san-agustin-megaliths, claim TL:COL:event:1bce:san-agustin-megaliths, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tierradentro tombs
claims.summary: The people of Tierradentro hew vast painted underground burial chambers into the mountains, a unique record of a developed pre-Hispanic Andean society.

claims.summary: The Muisca chiefdoms flourish on the high plateau around Bogota and Tunja, celebrated for goldwork, salt, and trade across the Andes.
